subject: Discovery Recap: Migration off proprietary LLM APIs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechinc.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery Recap: Migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Alex — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps. Feel free to correct me if I missed anything.

High-level goal
- Evaluate migration off OpenAI/Anthropic APIs to a mix of open/third-party models hosted by Redwood to reduce per-token costs and avoid single-vendor lock-in while maintaining response quality and compliance.

Pain points you shared
- Cost: current spend on OpenAI embeddings/generation has grown ~3x year-over-year and is unpredictable.
- Latency & tail latency: some production inference (user-facing chat, summarization) needs 200-500ms p95 for short responses; long context summarization can tolerate higher but still sensitive.
- Compliance & data residency: PCI scope and strict audit log/KMS requirements; need SOC2 evidence and isolation for sensitive flows.
- Compatibility: existing codepaths expect OpenAI-style APIs and streaming; minimum changes preferred.
- Quality regression risk: they need confidence model outputs remain at least as good as current baseline for your core intents (accounting reconciliation, transaction summarization, customer support triage).

Current stack we discussed
- OpenAI for chat and embeddings (prod); Anthropic for some instruction-following tests.
- Orchestration: internal router that tags requests by intent and routes to whichever provider; some protobuf wrappers around OpenAI calls.
- Evaluation: in-house evals + a few black-box A/B tests.

Success criteria for a pilot
- Comparable or better accuracy on 3 prompt families (chat assist, long-context summarization, embeddings for semantic search).
- <2x current latency at p95 for short chat flows; target 200-500ms depending on model; clear cost-per-1k-token improvement target (we discussed aiming for ~30-50% cost reduction).
- SOC2 + audit logs + KMS integration for keys; VPC/private deployment option acceptable for higher-sensitivity flows.

Model shortlist (initial)
- Redwood-1 (quantized variant) — our fast lower-cost candidate
- Mistral-instruct (preferred open instruct model)
- Llama 2 / Meta family (70B Q4 quantized variant) for longer-context/high-quality cases
- Falcon / Mosaic models for some instruction cases

Compatibility notes
- Redwood exposes OpenAI-compatible endpoints and SDKs; most of your existing wrappers should work with minimal changes (streaming, function-calling support included).

Proposed next steps
1) Sign an NDA so we can exchange a small evaluation dataset and more detailed SOC artifacts (I’ll send a DocuSign link).
2) Redwood provides a pilot SOW + dedicated pilot environment (can be hosted Private or Dedicated) — draft attached.
3) Technical deep-dive with infra + applied ML (Aditya & Rishi to join) to define dataset, traffic shaping, and evaluation metrics. I’ve linked a calendar slot below — propose Tue 2026-06-30 10am PT.
4) We’ll provide an initial perf/cost estimate and a short test harness for your team to run the three prompt families.

Attachments: redwood-product-sheet.pdf (product/architecture overview), pilot-sow-draft.docx (draft SOW).

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the DocuSign NDA and a calendar invite.
—
Marissa Cole
VP, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechinc.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Compliance: we need SOC2 Type II; PCI scope reduction is a hard ask. Can Redwood host the customer in a VPC with customer-controlled KMS? We also need sample audit logs for request-level metadata (who, when, model, prompt hash).

2) Perf targets: the 200-500ms p95 is realistic for our short flows (single-turn chat, ~80-150 tokens output). For long-context summarization (2k–10k tokens context), latency is secondary but throughput/sequence cost is important.

3) Model shortlist: your suggestions look good — we’d like to test (a) Redwood-1 quantized, (b) Mistral-instruct (latest), and (c) Llama2-70B Q4 quantized. For embeddings we’ll need cosine-compatible vectors (OpenAI-like dims) or mapping guidance.

4) Data for pilot: we can share a de-identified dataset of ~2k prompts/examples and a small eval harness. I’ll attach our security requirements doc and a short priority list.

Attachments: security_requirements.xlsx

If you can send the NDA link and the pilot SOW, we’ll get legal/infra to review. Tue 6/30 10am PT works for the technical deep-dive — Aditya and one infra engineer will join.

—
Alex
Head of Platform | Fintech Inc.
alex.johnson@fintechinc.com | +1 (212) 555-0142

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechinc.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Thanks Alex — appreciate the details and the attachment. Quick answers and follow-ups below.

Compliance & hosting
- We can offer Dedicated pools with VPC peering and customer-managed KMS (HSM-backed options available for enterprise plans). We’ll provide SOC2 Type II report and a sample audit-log export (request-level metadata including timestamps, model, request id, route). I’ll attach the SOC2 packet in a follow-up to your legal contact.

Latency & perf
- For the short-chat band (80–150 tokens) we expect p95 in the 150–400ms range on our Redwood-1 quantized profile on our Dedicated GPUs; long-context runs will vary by model but we’ll provide baseline numbers during the pilot. We’ll also instrument tail latency and provide per-route dashboards.

Embeddings
- We support OpenAI-like embeddings shapes and can return cosine-normalized vectors or raw floats; we’ll include a short script for mapping if you must match existing vector dims.

Pilot logistics
- I’ve attached a draft pilot SOW (pilot-sow-draft.docx). Next steps I’ll initiate:
  * Send NDA (DocuSign): https://www.docusign.com/prepare/ABC123
  * HubSpot record (for internal tracking): https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/contact/7654321
  * Calendar: technical deep-dive Tue 2026-06-30 10:00 PT — https://cal.com/marissa/technical-deep-dive?date=2026-06-30

For the technical deep-dive, Aditya and Rishi will cover production integration and evaluation metrics. Can you confirm the dataset delivery timeline (we discussed sending within 48–72 hours after NDA)?

Attachments: redwood-product-sheet.pdf (again), pilot-sow-draft.docx

—
Marissa
